title: Ezekiel Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came unto me
Prophesy against the mountains of Israel
I will bring a sword upon you
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto me
questions.explanation: This is the first event stated in the chapter, as seen in Ezekiel 6:1.

questions.question: To whom did the word of the LORD come?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel, as noted in Ezekiel 6:1.

questions.question: What was Ezekiel commanded to set his face toward?
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Ezekiel 6:2, where it says 'set thy face toward the mountains of Israel'.

questions.question: What does the Lord GOD say He will bring upon the mountains of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 states that the Lord GOD will bring a sword upon the mountains of Israel.

questions.question: What will happen to the high places according to the Lord GOD?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 states that the Lord GOD will destroy the high places.

questions.question: What will happen to the altars?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:4 indicates that the altars shall be desolate.

questions.question: What will happen to the images according to the prophecy?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:4 states that the images shall be broken.

questions.question: What will be laid before the idols?
options: The dead carcasses of the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The dead carcasses of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:5 mentions that the dead carcasses of the children of Israel will be laid before their idols.

questions.question: What will happen to the bones of the children of Israel?
options: They will be scattered round about the altars
questions.correctAnswer: They will be scattered round about the altars
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:5 states that the bones will be scattered round about the altars.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the 'Son of man' in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is referred to as 'Son of man' in Ezekiel 6:2.

questions.question: The word of the Lord GOD is directed to which geographical features?
options: The mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys
questions.correctAnswer: The mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 specifically addresses the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys of Israel.

questions.question: According to the text, the altars will be desolate.
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Ezekiel 6:4 where it states 'your altars shall be desolate'.

questions.question: The Lord GOD will bring a flood upon the mountains of Israel.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention a flood; it states that the Lord GOD will bring a sword upon the mountains of Israel in Ezekiel 6:3.

questions.question: Images shall be broken according to the prophecy.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:4 clearly states that 'your images shall be broken'.

questions.question: The children of Israel will be honored before their idols.
questions.explanation: The text states that the dead carcasses will be laid before their idols, not that they will be honored, as seen in Ezekiel 6:5.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the high places according to Ezekiel 6:6?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:6 states, 'the high places shall be desolate.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 6:2 promise will happen if someone prophesies against the mountains of Israel?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:3 says, 'I will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.'

questions.question: What shall happen to the slain according to Ezekiel 6:7?
options: They shall fall in the midst of you
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall in the midst of you
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:7 states, 'the slain shall fall in the midst of you.'

questions.question: What will the remnant do according to Ezekiel 6:9?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:9 states, 'they that escape of you shall remember me among the nations.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 6:10, what will the people know?
options: That they are the chosen ones
That the Lord has not spoken in vain
questions.correctAnswer: That the Lord has not spoken in vain
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:10 states, 'And they shall know that I am the LORD, and that I have not said in vain.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 6:4 indicate will happen to the altars?
options: They shall be filled with sacrifices
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:4 states, 'your altars shall be desolate.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 6:8 suggest about the fate of those who escape?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:8 mentions, 'when ye shall be scattered through the countries.'

questions.question: What is described in Ezekiel 6:5 regarding the children of Israel?
options: Their carcasses will be laid before idols
questions.correctAnswer: Their carcasses will be laid before idols
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:5 states, 'I will lay the dead carcases of the children of Israel before their idols.'

questions.question: What does the phrase 'whorish heart' in Ezekiel 6:9 imply about the people's actions?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as the term 'whorish heart' indicates a departure from loyalty to God, reflecting rebellion against Him.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 6:3 relate to the punishment mentioned in Ezekiel 6:6?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:3 states that prophesying against the mountains leads to the destruction mentioned in 6:6.

questions.question: What is the main consequence of idolatry mentioned in Ezekiel 6:9?
options: They will loathe themselves for their evils
questions.correctAnswer: They will loathe themselves for their evils
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Ezekiel 6:9 states they shall 'lothe themselves for the evils.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 6:10, what does the Lord's promise indicate about His intentions?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Ezekiel 6:10 states that He has not spoken in vain, indicating His promises are serious.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 6:6 indicates that the cities will be restored.
questions.explanation: This is false because Ezekiel 6:6 states that the cities shall be laid waste.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 6:7 assures that the slain will know the Lord.
questions.explanation: This is true as Ezekiel 6:7 states, 'and ye shall know that I am the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 6:8 promises that the remnant will have a prosperous future without struggle.
questions.explanation: This is false because Ezekiel 6:8 indicates that they will escape the sword but will be scattered among the nations.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 6.

questions.question: What action does the Lord God instruct Ezekiel to perform in Ezekiel 6:11?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:11 states, 'Thus saith the Lord GOD; Smite with thine hand, and stamp with thy foot...', indicating the specific actions commanded by God.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 6:12, what will happen to those who are far off?
options: They shall die of the pestilence
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die of the pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:12 says, 'He that is far off shall die of the pestilence...', clarifying the fate of those distanced from the calamities.

questions.question: What will the slain men be found among, according to Ezekiel 6:13?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:13 mentions, 'when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars...', highlighting the consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to do to the land in Ezekiel 6:14?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:14 states, 'So will I stretch out my hand upon them, and make the land desolate...', indicating the severity of God's judgment.

questions.question: What phrase signifies the ultimate recognition of the Lord's authority in Ezekiel 6:7?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:7 concludes with, 'and ye shall know that I am the LORD.', emphasizing the acknowledgment of God's sovereignty.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'abominations' in Ezekiel 6:11 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'abominations' refers to acts that provoke disgust and rejection by God, indicating severe wrongdoing.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Ezekiel 6:7 with the phrase 'ye shall know that I am the LORD'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'ye shall know that I am the LORD' is repeated throughout the book of Ezekiel, emphasizing the theme of recognition of God's authority.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment for idolatry found in Ezekiel 6:4?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 44:3 discusses the consequences of idolatry, thus connecting with the judgment theme in Ezekiel 6:4.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the promise of a remnant as seen in Ezekiel 6:8?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:5 speaks of a remnant of believers, paralleling the promise of a remnant in Ezekiel 6:8.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Ezekiel 6:11?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:10 discusses God's intent to bring judgment, directly leading into the lamentation in verse 11.

questions.question: What follows Ezekiel 6:12 in the narrative?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:13 follows with a description of the aftermath of judgment, emphasizing the seriousness of the situation.

questions.question: The term 'whorish heart' in Ezekiel 6:9 reflects what aspect of Israel's behavior?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'whorish heart' in Ezekiel 6:9 signifies Israel's unfaithfulness to God through idolatry.

questions.question: The phrase 'fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence' in Ezekiel 6:11 is an example of what literary device?
questions.explanation: The structure of the phrase shows parallelism as it presents three forms of judgment in a balanced manner.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 6:14 emphasizes the theme of God's mercy over judgment.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:14 emphasizes desolation and judgment rather than mercy, indicating God's fury as part of His judgment.

questions.question: True or False: The theme of recognition of the Lord's sovereignty is prominent in Ezekiel 6.
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase 'ye shall know that I am the LORD' throughout Ezekiel 6 reinforces the theme of God's sovereignty.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 6:3 teach about God's judgment on human sin?
options: God will bring destruction upon idolatry and false worship
God rewards those who build high places
God ignores sins committed in mountains and hills
God only judges cities, not natural places
questions.correctAnswer: God will bring destruction upon idolatry and false worship
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 states that God will bring a sword upon the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys and will destroy their high places, showing His judgment against idolatry.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine justice is taught in Ezekiel 6:11?
options: God's justice is enacted through sword, famine, and pestilence
God's justice is only symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice is enacted through sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:11 declares that the house of Israel will fall by the sword, famine, and pestilence, illustrating the means of divine justice for their abominations.

questions.question: What doctrine about repentance and remembrance is taught in Ezekiel 6:9?
options: The remnant will remember God and loathe their sins after judgment
The remnant will forget God and continue in sin
God's remembrance is conditional on human perfection
Repentance is unnecessary for the scattered remnant
questions.correctAnswer: The remnant will remember God and loathe their sins after judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:9 describes that those who escape will remember God among the nations and loathe themselves for their evils, emphasizing repentance after judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 6:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:7 emphasizes that the slain will fall in the midst of Israel so that they will know that the LORD is God, demonstrating His sovereign power over life and death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 6:10 through God's fulfillment of His word?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:10 states that God has not spoken in vain and will accomplish the evil He declared, showing His faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 6:14 connect to the broader biblical theme of land desolation due to sin?
options: It reflects the covenantal curse upon the land for Israel's idolatry
It predicts the permanent blessing of the land
It denies any connection between sin and land devastation
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the covenantal curse upon the land for Israel's idolatry
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:14 speaks of making the land more desolate than wilderness, consistent with covenantal curses for disobedience found in Deuteronomy.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 6:8 anticipate the redemptive-historical theme of a remnant preserved by God?
options: God preserves a remnant to ensure future restoration
The remnant is self-sufficient apart from God
No remnant is mentioned in this chapter
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a remnant to ensure future restoration
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:8 promises a remnant left to escape the sword, aligning with biblical themes of God preserving a faithful remnant for restoration (cf. Isaiah 10:20-22).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 6:4 and 6:5 teach about idolatry and divine judgment?
options: Idolatry provokes God to destroy altars and scatter the bones of the dead around them
Idolatry is tolerated if accompanied by sacrifices
God ignores idolatry if the people repent immediately
Idolatry results in prosperity and blessing
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry provokes God to destroy altars and scatter the bones of the dead around them
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 describe God's judgment by desolating altars, breaking images, and scattering bones, showing the severe consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine wrath and knowledge of God is taught by Ezekiel 6:12 and 6:13?
options: God's wrath results in death by pestilence, sword, and famine so that people will know He is the LORD
God's wrath is random and unrelated to knowledge of Him
God's wrath leads to immediate forgiveness without consequences
God's wrath is only a metaphor for political struggles
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath results in death by pestilence, sword, and famine so that people will know He is the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:12-13 explain that the forms of punishment lead to the knowledge of God's identity and authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Ezekiel 6:6 and 6:14 provide about the consequences of Israel’s idolatry on their land and worship practices?
options: Idolatry leads to desolation of cities, altars, and land, abolishing their religious works
Idolatry enhances the prosperity and sanctity of the land
Idolatry is only punished in the cities but not the land
Idolatry results in additional altars and images being built
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry leads to desolation of cities, altars, and land, abolishing their religious works
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:6 and 6:14 describe the desolation of cities, altars, land, and religious works, showing the comprehensive consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Ezekiel 6:2-7 only depicts human warfare and not divine judgment. What does Ezekiel 6:2-7 actually teach?
options: It teaches that God Himself brings judgment resulting in destruction and death to demonstrate His sovereignty
It only describes human political conflicts without divine involvement
It suggests that the destruction is accidental and unrelated to sin
It promises that idols will protect Israel from harm
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God Himself brings judgment resulting in destruction and death to demonstrate His sovereignty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:2-7 explicitly states the word of the LORD commanding judgment on Israel’s mountains and idols, showing God's active role in judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 6:9 specifically teach about the human response to divine discipline?
options: True repentance includes remembering God and abhorring past sins
Discipline results in continued rebellion and pride
Divine discipline is always rejected by the remnant
Human response is irrelevant to God's purposes
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance includes remembering God and abhorring past sins
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:9 states that those who escape will remember God and loathe themselves for their abominations, indicating repentance as a response to discipline.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 6:14 particularly reveal about God’s response to persistent sin?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:14 shows God stretching out His hand to make the land desolate due to sin, revealing His holiness which cannot tolerate sin.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 6:8 illustrate God’s providential care amidst judgment?
options: God preserves a remnant to fulfill His redemptive promises
God’s judgment is indiscriminate and final
No remnant is mentioned in the chapter
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a remnant to fulfill His redemptive promises
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:8 states God will leave a remnant to escape the sword, showing His providence and faithfulness to preserve His covenant people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God’s holy justice and human responsibility is taught by Ezekiel 6:3 and 6:10?
options: God punishes idolatry as a just response and His word to do so is sure
God overlooks idolatry if people claim innocence
Idolatry is excused if performed in remote locations
God’s threats are empty and lack follow-through
questions.correctAnswer: God punishes idolatry as a just response and His word to do so is sure
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 pronounces judgment on idolatrous places and 6:10 affirms God will fulfill His declared punishment, demonstrating justice and faithfulness.
